hlni.insight: A task label alone does not define assessment; you must identify the criteria and feedback loop.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles inherently reveal the nature of the academic work.
hlni.viewerChange: Students will now audit specific assignment criteria before choosing a program.
hlni.support: The three-column audit separates task, criteria, and feedback, preventing assumptions about course content.
hlni.payoff: The audit exposes missing information, prompting a specific, actionable question about grading rubrics.

candidate.reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: The Assessment Audit
candidate.creativeAngle: Audit your academic tasks instead of relying on degree names.
candidate.objective: Enable students to evaluate degrees by auditing assessment criteria.
candidate.targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Confusion
shots.visual: Student holding two papers labelled B.Com and BBA, looking confused.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA? Don't just look at the degree name.

shots.name: The Audit
shots.visual: Student writing on a three-column worksheet.
shots.dialogue: Audit the tasks. Example: Task: Analyze costs. Graded on: ? Feedback: ?
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Analyze costs. Graded on: ? Feedback: ?
shots.cameraPerformance: Over-the-shoulder shot focusing on the writing.

shots.name: The Result
shots.dialogue: The unknown is your answer. Ask: What specific grading rubric is used for this assignment?
shots.onscreenText: What specific grading rubric is used for this assignment?

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use a three-column audit to identify missing grading information instead of assuming degree content.

selected.title: The Assessment Audit
selected.audienceGap: Students assume a course name defines the entire assessment experience.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Learns to look for assessment criteria rather than just titles.
selected.concept: A student compares two sample tasks from different sources without assumptions.
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: Two sample tasks: 'Financial Analysis Report' vs 'Market Entry Strategy'
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Analyze costs. Graded on: ? Feedback: ?
demonstration.observation: Student marks question marks on criteria and feedback columns.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific grading rubric is used for this assignment?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = assessment_questions / three_column_audit; Connection = task_question_journal / student_journal_reflection; Discovery = insufficient_information / missing_source_check. Each has an illustrative input, observable result and next question. This is not editorial approval.

qa.failureReason: fidelity: In the hook, the student holds two papers labeled B.Com and BBA, which implies the video is a comparison between degrees rather than a method for auditing any assessment. Revision: Change the paper labels to 'Task A' and 'Task B' to align with the method of auditing tasks rather than comparing degree brands. payoff: The payoff mentions the student circling the question marks, but does not show how this action shifts the viewer's next step from a vague preference to a concrete inquiry process. Revision: Include a visual transition showing the student using the circled questions to initiate an inquiry, demonstrating the transition from assumption to information-seeking.
